shower.thought: # Original Shower Thoughts
People spend years perfecting their appearance for strangers, but the people closest to them see them at their worst.
You only know you've lived long enough when you start recognizing patterns in your own mistakes.
The fear of missing out wouldn't exist if we could actually see the futures we didn't choose.
Most of us are just one conversation away from completely changing our minds about someone.
Time moves slower when you're waiting for something and faster when you're dreading it, which means our perception of time is just measuring our resistance to the present.
You can't prove you're intelligent to someone determined to think you're stupid, but you also can't prove you're stupid to someone determined to think you're intelligent.
Forgetting someone's name mid-conversation is the social equivalent of your computer freezing while they're watching.
We treat our bodies like we're going to trade them in for a new model, but we only get this one.
The moment you stop needing someone's approval is usually the moment you finally get it.
Every friendship starts with two people pretending to be slightly more interesting versions of themselves.
You've probably given someone advice that completely changed their life, and you'll never know it.
The things you'd never admit to thinking are probably the most human things about you.
Money is just a mutual agreement to pretend pieces of paper and numbers mean something, and somehow that's made the world function better.
You become an adult the moment you realize your parents were also just figuring it out as they went.
We spend the first half of our lives learning who we are and the second half learning who we're not.
The people who annoy you most are often showing you what you're afraid of becoming.
Nostalgia is just your brain cherry-picking the moments that made you feel alive.
You're the villain in someone else's story, and they're probably right about some of it.
The best conversations happen when you stop trying to convince someone and start trying to understand them.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my friend he needed to stop drinking so much.
He said, "You're right, I should probably start paying attention to my driving too."

My dad said, "Son, I'm disappointed in you."
I said, "Join the club. We meet on Thursdays."

I went to a wedding last weekend.
Two families became one, and somehow we all lost money.

My therapist asked what my biggest fear is.
I said, "Becoming like my father."
She said, "You're already here every week."

I told my boss I was thinking about quitting.
He said, "Don't do anything rash."
I said, "I haven't yet."

My girlfriend asked if I believed in love at first sight.
I said, "No, but I believe in regret at first argument."

I asked my accountant if I was spending too much money.
He said, "Not anymore."

At my high school reunion, everyone asked what I'd been up to.
I said, "Mostly staying out of the news."

My doctor said I need to cut back on sugar.
I said, "Doc, at this point, my blood type is practically caramel."

I went to a motivational speaker who said, "You miss 100% of the shots you don't take."
Turns out that's also true for suicide hotline calls.

My wife asked why I never remember our anniversary.
I said, "Because I want to remember our marriage."

I told my kid, "Life is like a box of chocolates."
He said, "No it isn't, that's from a movie."
I said, "Exactly."

My trainer said, "No pain, no gain."
My back said, "How about just pain?"

I asked my friend how his divorce was going.
He said, "Great! I'm finally happy again."
Turns out he meant his ex-wife.

A priest, a rabbi, and a therapist walk into a bar.
The bartender asks, "What'll it be?"
They all say, "Whatever helps us forget."

I visited my parents last week.
My mom said, "You never call."
My dad said nothing.
Progress.

My date asked, "Do you believe in soulmates?"
I said, "No, but I believe in settling."
She said, "That's actually more honest than most guys."

I asked my friend why he stopped going to the gym.
He said, "I realized I was just delaying the inevitable."

My kid asked why I seemed so sad.
I said, "Because I realized you're going to make all the same mistakes I did."
He said, "What mistakes?"
I said, "That's the spirit."

My boss asked if I was happy at my job.
I said, "Happiness seems like an unrealistic expectation."
He said, "Welcome to management."
